title: MultiSelect/SelectBase normalizes react-select's null onChange for multi-select
answers: Why does removing the last tag/option crash my multi-select handler?
Do I need to handle null from onChange in a MultiSelect consumer?
react-select passes null when the last multi-value is removed
body: Invariant: react-select calls onChange with `null` (not `[]`) when the last value is removed from a multi-select. SelectBase already normalizes this for isMulti before handing the value to react-select/consumers (packages/grafana-ui/src/components/Select/SelectBase.tsx:218-226, onChangeWithEmpty), so components built on MultiSelect (e.g. TagFilter in notebook's NotebookDocumentHeader) receive `[]`, never `null`, and must not call `.forEach`/array methods defensively assuming null. If you consume raw react-select directly (bypassing SelectBase), you still need to normalize null yourself.
applies: Any component using grafana-ui MultiSelect/SelectBase for multi-value selects, e.g. notebook tag editing.

search: MultiSelect/SelectBase normalizes react-select's null onChange to [] for multi-select values before passing to consumers. React-select calls onChange with null (not []) when the last value is removed, but SelectBase already handles this normalization (packages/grafana-ui/src/components/Select/SelectBase.tsx:218-226, onChangeWithEmpty) so components like TagFilter in notebook's NotebookDocumentHeader receive [] and must not call array methods defensively assuming null. If consuming raw react-select directly (bypassing SelectBase), you must normalize null yourself. Applies to any component using grafana-ui MultiSelect/SelectBase for multi-value selects; see public/app/features/notebook/scene/layout-notebook/NotebookDocumentHeader.test.tsx for context.
